name: Ideaspring Capital
identity_check: Ideaspring Capital (also written IdeaSpring) at ideaspringcap.com: a Bengaluru early-stage VC (head office in Jayanagar, Bengaluru), set up in 2016. Its founder and managing partner is Naganand Doraswamy. Confirmed by the domain, the firm's own About, Contact and team pages, and press (Mint and Moneycontrol on the 2016 launch; YourStory and VCCircle on its rounds). It is not Aarin Capital, Fund I's anchor investor (Mohandas Pai's firm). It is also not Patni Financial Advisors or Nirvana Venture Advisors, the other firms of Venture Partner Arihant Patni.

thesis_text.value: Bengaluru early-stage fund that leads rounds in science- and IP-led B2B product startups building from India for global markets, often at prototype or pre-revenue stage. Focus areas: AI-powered enterprise software, biotech and life sciences, and deep tech (semiconductors, quantum, space, robotics, defence, climate). Offers hands-on product and engineering help through an in-house CTO. Fund III initial cheques ₹10–20 Cr.

open_items: Only 3 of the 10 rounds fall in the last 24 months: HrdWyr (May 2026), Litemed/Curapod (Feb 2026) and GrowthPal (Jan 2026). No round announcement was found for these Fund II deep-tech companies: LatentForce (agentic AI for code migration, IISc), Accelequant (quantum), Phyx44, Gyrophint, Tvaster Genkalp, Kcat Enzymatic, SmartShip, Gooru, Mason, Ambee. The web-search budget ran out. Entrackr and Inc42 had no usable tag pages for the firm. Economic Times could not be fetched (this includes the ET BluJ article linked from blujaero.com/news).

US-domiciled (flipped) companies: no stated policy found. The site says it invests in companies 'based in India and building for the world' and stresses an India–US corridor. India Deep Tech Alliance founding members (Ideaspring is one, Sep 2025) commit capital to 'Indian-domiciled' deep-tech companies. A homepage testimonial styles a portfolio company 'Spanugo Inc.', which hints at a US entity, but this is not confirmed. requires_us_entity = 'no' means only that a US entity is not required.

Industrial / manufacturing is not a stated sector. Nearest signals: Partner Kailashnath MS covers robotics and deep tech; Fund III themes name robotics and advanced materials; HrdWyr targets industrial markets; Simyog does EMI/EMC simulation for hardware design; Kcat engineers enzymes for industrial chemistry. 'AI agents for factory operations' would fall under the 'AI-powered enterprise software' theme, but the firm does not say so.

Fund III: target ₹750 Cr (Apr 2026 blog); its first portfolio company is HrdWyr. No first- or final-close announcement was found. VCCircle (14 Oct 2026) lists Ideaspring Capital among the 14 PE/VC second-level fund managers chosen for the ₹1 trillion RDI Fund; the amount and vehicle are undisclosed.

Inbound nuance: the site invites pitches by email and Google Form, but the 2026 blog says its most distinctive companies came through institutional relationships (IISc, BIRAC/C-CAMP, iDEX, IITs) rather than inbound pitches.
Fund I anchor LP was Aarin Capital (Mint, Moneycontrol 2016). SIDBI and BIRAC fund-of-funds support is acknowledged in the 2026 blog. LP commitments by fund are not disclosed.
SEBI AIF registration numbers were not checked.

Kailashnath MS's team page has an 'On Linkedin' label but no link, so linkedin_url is null. Venture Partner Arihant Patni, Venture Advisor Dr Ajith Kamath (biotech) and VP Sulesh Kumar are left out as not specific to industrial / AI / hardware.
Litemed: press reports the round under the product brand 'Curapod'. Ideaspring's portfolio page links Curapod to Litemed. HQ country was not stated in the round article.
GrowthPal and ClearTrust: HQ not stated in the round articles. GrowthPal's round stage is not stated, and the participating 'global angel investors' are unnamed.

The 2026 blog says 10 of 17 Fund II companies raised follow-on rounds, but the portfolio page tags only 15 companies as Fund II. Exits marked on the site: Bewgle, Numocity, Peritus AI, Spanugo, Whodat, Zapty.
